claims.note: Re-recorded 24 August at scoring 15 on the **M1 Pro** at --runs 3, because SCORING_VERSION 15 (#554) is a declared invalidation trigger and refused the 19 August v14 recording. Nothing moved: across all 62 development fixtures the three runs agreed on every step score, end-to-end score and review rate, and validation enforces that — a baseline recording a moved spread downgrades its claim. Two things changed with the machine rather than the measurement. The run is local rather than the rented 5090 the v14 recording used, so the *timing* (33m54s) is this machine's and only the scores carry over; evals/RENTED-GPU.md is explicit that cross-backend score equivalence is asserted and never measured, and this is the first of these two claims to stand on Metal. And the sidecar string moved from `10145 (ad256ded)` to `10145 (ad256ded3)` — the same llama.cpp build, printed with one more character of its hash, which the exact-match content check (#489) reads as a change. Recorded here so the next reader does not take it for one. The confidence signal on this pack remains INVERTED: `high` errs at 0.02 over 331 decisions where `low` errs at 0.00 over 339, so routing the less confident decisions to review spends the review on the wrong ones (#429). That is a property this claim does not assert and does not need.

claims.wording: kettle mutate's exit code means something new survived: the renewal pack's expected survivors are declared with counts and reasons in packs/app.kttl.renewal-diff/expected-survivors.json, and an undeclared survivor family or a declared family over its count fails the run.

claims.note: The v14 census of 12 August 2026 is 349 survivors in the two declared families — 261 ceiling-tolerated single errors, 88 already-contained claims — with no remainder and no overlap; v13's was 261 (237 + 24), the growth tracking #493's referral fixtures and the oracle now answering them (#484). Killed keeps its strict meaning (gate failure, for scoring-contained operators), and item-level detection prints as a second, separate number, never a kill: wrong_value_from_multi_value_quote kills 0 of its 273 sites and has no gate path at all at these denominators. Two caveats travel with the declaration itself: force_confidence_high has no sites because the oracle answers all-high (a coverage gap, not a clean sweep), and family 1's Wilson headroom constant is #448-era arithmetic on a smaller bed — the mechanism is re-confirmed, the constants are not.

claims.wording: The confidence shown beside a finding predicts whether it is right: a finding marked settled is likelier to be correct than one marked unsure.
invalidation: a calibration measurement on this pack
removal of the confidence tag from the report
claims.review_route: grow the bed until the medium bucket can carry a bound, then re-measure: kettle eval app.kttl.subscription-audit --model <weights>, reading the `confidence /` block (#429). The 14 August run is archived and replayable, so a scoring change costs no GPU.
claims.note: **The trigger fired on 17 August 2026: #519 took the graded tag off the report, and this entry is where that was declared to be checkable.** What came off is the grade — the tag now reads SETTLED or UNSURE, `ConfidenceView::build` in render.rs no longer prints the model's word, and the disclosure asks "Why this one is unsure" rather than quoting a rank back at the reader. The app's evidence row lost its High/Medium/Low tag entirely. What did not change is this claim's sentence, which was already written in the two states rather than the three grades: a settled row still asserts more than an unsure one, the derivation is still `matches!(confidence, Confidence::High)`, and nothing has measured whether that predicts anything on this pack. So the status stays unproven and the review route is unchanged — a narrower surface is not evidence, exactly as removing the landing-page copy was not. The reason for cutting the grade was that #429 measured it on the two neighbouring packs and the product went on displaying it: the registry is published beside the app now, and a rank the measurements call noise is the first contradiction a careful reader would find. **Measured 14 August and still unproven — but no longer unmeasured, and the direction is the opposite of what the other packs show.** Replaying the rented-GPU subscription run of that afternoon through the per-question confidence split: high 0.10 error over 48 asserted decisions (95% CI 0.05–0.22), medium 0.43 over 14 (0.21–0.67), and low undefined because all 40 of its decisions were routed to review rather than asserted. High to medium points the right way — more confident, less wrong — and the intervals overlap, so this bed cannot establish it. Verdict UNPROVEN. The first reading of that same run said INVERTED, and the instrument was at fault: the error rate divided by *all* decisions including routed ones, so a wholly routed bucket scored a guaranteed 0.00 and everything ranked against it. #429 had already named the right denominator — error among automatically asserted items — and it had not been implemented. What would prove this claim is a bigger bed rather than a better model: 14 asserted medium decisions cannot carry a Wilson bound. Surfaces emptied 14 August, after the entry blocked the demo build — which is the mechanism working, not a fault in it: app/vite.demo.config.ts runs kettle claims at build time, so a public page cannot be published while its copy stands on an unproven claim. The landing page's "Kettle marks what it is not sure enough to count" was the general predictive claim and is gone; what the report is left doing is narrower and true, giving a reason about a finding's own evidence ("Four payments three months apart looks quarterly, but some energy plans smooth payments differently"). Displaying a declared level beside a stated reason is not the same assertion as this claim's sentence, so the report template and the demo fixture came off with it. What would put them back: any copy presenting the tag as a reliability signal rather than a label on a stated reason. The claim stays recorded and unproven — removing the copy is not evidence, and the measurement is still owed. Recorded because the surface exists and the claim did not. Until 17 August 2026 the subscription report rendered a HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW tag taken straight from the model's declared level — render.rs derives `settled` as `matches!(confidence, Confidence::High)` — and added a "Why only 'medium'" explanation beside it. fixtures/run-01/report.html carried five HIGH and two MEDIUM tags, and app/demo serves that file, so this was a public claim rather than an internal one. No assurance claim covered it, which meant no invalidation trigger could ever fire on it: it could not be downgraded because it had never been asserted. It is unproven rather than failed: nothing has measured it. There is no model-answer recording for this pack in kettle-runs or evals/runs — only --no-model runs — so it cannot be settled by replay and needs a GPU sitting. What is measured is the two neighbouring packs, on 14 August under scoring 14, and both came back negative: the letter pack declared `high` on all 476 decisions (NO RANKING SIGNAL, 24 of them wrong), and the renewal pack came back INVERTED — `high` carried all 8 errors across 342 decisions and `low` carried none across 339, so routing low-confidence decisions to review would spend 339 reviews and catch none of the errors. That separation is 0.0007 wide and one further error in `low` would withdraw it. Neither result transfers: they are different packs, different steps and different questions, and this entry must not be read as evidence against the sentence any more than for it. One corroborating detail from the mutation census: the `force_confidence_high` operator has no sites at all, because the oracle answers all-high — the harness cannot currently perturb this signal either.

claims.wording: The model does not learn from your documents: the weights are downloaded once against a pinned checksum, and from then on Kettle only ever reads them.
invalidation: a second writer of model files, for any reason
an adapter, fine-tune or training flag reaching the sidecar's argv
a pack step that writes anything back into the models directory
personalisation of any kind — a per-person file the pipeline reads and updates
claims.review_route: the two owning tests, and `crates/runner/src/sidecar.rs` for what the process is actually asked to do. Both scans are deliberately dumb — markers on lines of shipped source — so a reviewer can believe the answer without reading the scanner.
claims.note: Recorded because the question is asked of everything in this category and Kettle had never answered it in public. The trigger was an article describing on-device models as ones that "learn your habits" — a privacy promise pointing the wrong way, since a thing that learns your habits has to keep them. Kettle's answer is mechanical rather than a policy: `models.json` pins a sha256 the downloader checks, the file is opened to be read, and the process reading it is llama-server, an inference server given a model and a port. **What this does not prove**: it is a source scan, the same instrument and the same limits as the network boundary next door (#233). It shows that no call site was added; it cannot see what a dependency does on its own thread, and it says nothing about a packaged release's runtime behaviour. Scope is macOS because that is the only platform with a shipped sidecar. The claim is deliberately about learning, not about privacy in general — what leaves the machine is `no-non-loopback-network`'s question, and it remains unproven at runtime for want of a packaged capture. No public surface cites this yet: the sentence goes on kttl.app only once somebody wants it there, and this entry is what makes it citable rather than merely true.
